takeaway: The radar measured GitHub through its API for the first time: 2,045 readings, exact counts, and the registry grew from 213 to 1,191 apps. The newest fast mover is DeepSeek's own agent repo, 4,615 stars on its first day.

findings.heading: GitHub measured by API for the first time
findings.text: The topic search returned 2,045 readings and the remaining repos on the recheck list were re-read with exact counts. A fifth of the evidence behind the top 25 is now the radar's own API measurement, up from none.

findings.heading: DeepSeek's agent repo: 4,615 stars on day one
findings.text: deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype, 'Towards a More Autonomous Agent System', was created on Oct 31 and has 426 forks.

findings.heading: Seventh forecast: a weaker week
findings.text: The Oct 25 ranking scored a rank correlation of 0.61 and got 40% of its top 15 right (73% the day before). It ranked apps on gains stated days earlier and missed the design skills and claude-mem that took off after it.

findings.heading: t3code accelerates for a fourth day
findings.text: pingdotgg/t3code gained 3,163 stars in a day (33,060 to 36,223), after 320, 849 and 971.

findings.heading: Design skills keep coming
findings.text: heydamir/unslop, a Claude skill that turns AI-looking UI into a designed interface, reached 3,979 stars three days after it was created.

caveats: Repos found by the API bring raw GitHub topics as tags, so today's direction table (236 directions) and its 83 rule hypotheses are mostly noise.
About 168 repos came in through generic search terms that are now filtered out; they stay in the registry, low in the ranking.
Seven matured forecasts are still a small sample; the tuner's bar keeps noise-sized gains from moving any setting.
Hugging Face and Hacker News remain unreachable from the cloud environment.
